title: Enterprise infrastructure: Integration benefits increase dependence
desc: Balances connected agentic execution and specified review against governance fragility and vendor lock-in.

kps.k: The cluster frames legal AI as governed enterprise infrastructure, not simply a more capable model.
kps.d: Google argues that confidentiality, ethical walls and matter permissions require a system combining firm-specific instructions, connections to existing legal systems, executable agents and centralized governance. Freshfields’ adoption narrative similarly places Gemini inside bespoke legal platforms and everyday work tools. The substantive proposition is that integration and institutional knowledge enable routine legal deployment; model intelligence alone does not.

qs.q: What makes the difference is the system built around the model: skills that enhance a firm's own expertise, connections into the systems where matters actually live, agents that complete work rather than return suggestions, and an open ecosystem to extend all of it — with governance running underneath all four**.
qs.a: Gemini Enterprise for Legal — Google Cloud's Legal Vertical Launch · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

qs.q: Since the collaboration launched, Freshfields has integrated Google’s Gemini models across multiple bespoke legal solutions developed by the Freshfields Lab.
qs.a: Freshfields Reports Google Cloud Collaboration Delivering Transformation at Scale · Law firms · 2026

kps.k: Agentic execution expands automation while retaining specified human review points.
kps.d: Google describes agents that monitor regulatory changes, compile personal data, review contracts, extract playbooks and draft documents. Its workflows retain practitioner review of policy drafts and confirmation of sensitive material before redaction, while reserving strategic negotiation and judgment for lawyers. This supports supervised workflow automation rather than unrestricted substitution. Claims of processing in seconds, faster turnaround and lower review overhead remain vendor assertions; the supplied material reports no measured accuracy or verification burden.

qs.q: **Unlocking high-value legal workflows**  By shifting from simple text generation to true agentic task execution, Gemini Enterprise for Legal automates and accelerates complex legal operations, including:  - **Proactive regulatory horizon scanning:** Keeps legal and compliance teams ahead of global mandates by autonomously tracking legislative updates, court dockets, and supervisory bodies.
qs.a: Gemini Enterprise for Legal — Google Cloud's Legal Vertical Launch · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

qs.q: It cross-references emerging changes against enterprise policies to flag exposure gaps and generate updated policy drafts for immediate practitioner review.
qs.a: Gemini Enterprise for Legal — Google Cloud's Legal Vertical Launch · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

kps.k: Governance promises depend on preserving controls across connected systems.
kps.d: Google claims inherited permissions, private organizational data excluded from foundation-model training, primary-authority grounding, traceable citations and audit logging. Partner accounts qualify how integration operates: Legora limits access to approved mutual customers and retains source controls, while Relativity says sensitive data and substantive analysis remain within its environment. These are architectural assurances, not independent demonstrations of security or legal accuracy. For adopters, the practical issue is how permissions, data boundaries and review responsibilities operate across the complete workflow.

qs.q: Because Gemini Enterprise for Legal runs on Google Cloud infrastructure and the Gemini Enterprise platform, the permissions and access controls your firm already maintains are the boundaries the platform operates within — not settings it asks you to reconstruct.
qs.a: Gemini Enterprise for Legal — Google Cloud's Legal Vertical Launch · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

qs.q: Legora has also announced that they will become a partner, and that ‘approved mutual customers will be able to utilise some Legora capabilities from within Gemini Enterprise, receiving responses and answers to queries that link back to the relevant Legora thread, where citations, source grounding and permissions remain in place’.
qs.a: Google Launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal · Market & press · 2026

kps.k: Freshfields supplies reported evidence of adoption at scale, but not quantified improvements in legal outcomes.
kps.d: The April 2025 account describes planned Google deployments and hoped-for due-diligence gains. By April 2026, Freshfields reports more than 5,000 professionals using Gemini-based tools, over 2,100 regular NotebookLM Enterprise users and over 2,800 Workspace users; these figures should not be added as distinct populations. It also reports bespoke-platform integrations, managed encryption keys and an AI Academy delivered by 260 AI Champions. This establishes reported implementation and uptake, not measured gains in accuracy, cost or client service. Nor does this earlier rollout validate the separate Gemini Enterprise for Legal product introduced in preview in August 2026.

qs.q: The tool is designed to enhance legal reviews and due diligence processes, which it hopes will improve its scale, accuracy, and efficiency - helping with the time-consuming and repetitive nature of due diligence processes that can be a drain on productivity for legal professionals and their clients.
qs.a: How Freshfields is Building a Multi-Agent AI Strategy for Legal Workflows with Google Cloud · Market & press · 2025

qs.q: Over 2,100 team members regularly use NotebookLM Enterprise to synthesize complex material and navigate large document sets more efficiently.
qs.a: Freshfields Reports Google Cloud Collaboration Delivering Transformation at Scale · Law firms · 2026

kps.k: The central strategic tension concerns integration benefits versus vendor dependence.
kps.d: Google argues that fragmented tools impose integration costs, that full-stack ownership improves cost-capacity economics and that its partner ecosystem avoids lock-in. Perez instead emphasizes separating cloud and AI procurement and maintaining multiple providers, including Google alongside Microsoft. The Linklaters strategy comparison interprets A&O Shearman’s Harvey relationship as deep integration with dependency risks, and Clifford Chance’s Microsoft approach as enterprise productivity with potentially less diversification. These are contrasting strategic judgments, not comparative performance findings; Freshfields’ Google partnership should not be read as an exclusive-stack commitment.

qs.q: Attempting to solve this by stitching together fragmented point-solutions or standalone models only creates a steep integration tax, resulting in fragile workflows.
qs.a: Gemini Enterprise for Legal — Google Cloud's Legal Vertical Launch · Legal-tech vendor · 2026

qs.q: ## Multi-vendor AI strategy**  Freshfields' approach to AI involves deliberately maintaining relationships with multiple AI providers rather than betting exclusively on any single platform.
qs.a: How Freshfields is Building a Multi-Agent AI Strategy for Legal Workflows with Google Cloud · Market & press · 2025

kps.k: Big Tech entry intensifies competition while also creating distribution channels for specialist providers.
kps.d: Artificial Lawyer interprets Google’s enterprise reach as an advantage in an increasingly competitive legal-AI market. Yet the launch connects Harvey, Legora, document-management systems and other specialist products rather than presenting a wholesale replacement for them; delivery partners also include consultants and ALSPs. The resulting model combines competition with partnership. The supplied material establishes announced relationships and market positioning, not market-share shifts, displacement or independently verified savings.

qs.q: As with Microsoft, Google is a true global player, integrated already into many companies via a range of needs – not the least the use of their Gemini LLMs.
qs.a: Google Launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal · Market & press · 2026

qs.q: The market to sell AI into legal enterprises has already become very competitive, this only adds to it.
qs.a: Google Launches Gemini Enterprise for Legal · Market & press · 2026

kps.k: Client acceptance and organizational capability can constrain adoption independently of technical readiness.
kps.d: Perez grounds technology selection in clients’ collaboration environments, including Workspace and Drive, but warns that internal proficiency does not ensure clients will accept AI-enabled services. Freshfields’ leadership-backed training and governance measures address implementation capacity; they do not by themselves establish client confidence. Across the cluster, customer endorsements mainly express expectations and intentions. The practical implication is to assess client demand and acceptance alongside integration, training and workflow controls, rather than treating deployment or usage as proof of service transformation.

qs.q: But we are seeing demand from our clients coming in, saying 'we are working on Google Workspace' or 'we are on Google Drive' and you need to be able to collaborate with them.
qs.a: How Freshfields is Building a Multi-Agent AI Strategy for Legal Workflows with Google Cloud · Market & press · 2025

qs.q: As an integral part of the firm’s rollout and adoption effort, Freshfields provided a comprehensive internal AI upskilling and training program, supported and endorsed by Freshfields leadership and partners.
qs.a: Freshfields Reports Google Cloud Collaboration Delivering Transformation at Scale · Law firms · 2026

vlens.an: These selected market-analysis, consultancy and press sources accept the proposition that legal AI’s practical value depends on integration into governed enterprise workflows rather than model capability alone. Common reasons include connections to specialist legal systems, agentic execution within existing work environments, centralized governance and reduced tool switching. They also materially develop the proposition by identifying concrete responses to integration risk: separating cloud and AI procurement, maintaining multiple providers and aligning technology choices with clients’ collaboration environments. Internal variation is material. The Linklaters strategy comparison directly frames deep integration and single-stack productivity as creating vendor dependency or reduced diversification; Artificial Lawyer emphasizes an integrated partner ecosystem and retained controls but does not substantiate lock-in risk or measured performance; the Freshfields report advances a deliberately multi-vendor, client-led strategy and notes that client acceptance may constrain adoption independently of technical readiness. Across these sources, productivity and quality improvements are generally expectations or vendor and adopter claims rather than comparative outcome evidence. This assessment concerns only the curated sources supplied and does not indicate how prevalent these views are among analysts, consultancies or the press generally.

qs.q: He added:  > Obviously AI is built on cloud, but you can definitely have a cloud provider, or multiple cloud providers, and even multiple AI providers.
qs.a: How Freshfields is Building a Multi-Agent AI Strategy for Legal Workflows with Google Cloud · Market & press · 2025

vlens.an: Freshfields supports the proposition that legal AI becomes useful as governed enterprise infrastructure rather than as a standalone model. Its account emphasizes integration into bespoke legal platforms and routine workflows, adoption at firmwide scale, managed security controls, leadership-backed training and daily use. These points reinforce the cluster’s claim that deployment depends on institutional systems and organizational capability. Material variation lies in what the source does not establish: the reported usage figures demonstrate uptake, not independently measured gains in accuracy, cost, efficiency or client outcomes; its security and service-transformation claims are organizational assertions; and it does not substantively examine verification burdens, cross-system governance fragility or vendor dependence. Accordingly, the source supports the integration-and-governance core of the proposition but provides limited evidence on its central trade-off between integration benefits and lock-in. This assessment applies to the supplied Freshfields source, not traditional law firms generally.

vlens.an: The supplied legal-tech vendor source supports the proposition that legal AI should be treated as governed enterprise infrastructure rather than as a standalone model. Google Cloud’s reasoning centres on permission-preserving connections to existing systems, firm-specific skills, centralized governance, and agents that execute workflows while retaining specified practitioner review points. It also argues that integration reduces the fragility and cost of fragmented tools. Material variation arises on the proposition’s dependence risk: Google presents broad partnerships and customization as means of avoiding vendor lock-in, while simultaneously promoting full-stack integration across infrastructure, models and applications. It therefore supports the cluster’s core infrastructure and integration claims but does not accept the downside as inevitable; its security, performance, cost and anti-lock-in claims remain vendor assertions rather than independent findings. Because this facet contains one curated vendor source, no wider prevalence or professional consensus can be inferred.

qs.q: What makes the difference is the system built around the model: skills that enhance a firm's own expertise, connections into the systems where matters actually live, agents that complete work rather than return suggestions, and an open ecosystem to extend all of it — with governance running underneath all four**.

qs.q: Partnerships with global systems integrators and legal-tech specialists — **Accenture**, **Deloitte**, **Devoteam**, **Factor Law**, **KPMG**, **Tribe.ai**, **Valtech**, **Zazmic**, **Zencore**, and **66degrees** — let organizations customize, integrate, and scale across complex enterprise architectures without vendor lock-in.

elens.an: The selected 2025 sources accept the proposition that legal AI becomes operationally useful through integration into enterprise systems and legal workflows, while deeper integration creates strategic dependence. They describe firm-wide productivity stacks, bespoke agents and due-diligence tooling as expected benefits, but largely report partnerships, plans and hoped-for gains rather than measured improvements in accuracy, cost or client outcomes. Collectively, they materially extend the proposition by identifying multi-vendor procurement and client-led technology selection as practical responses to lock-in: Freshfields separates cloud-provider choice from AI-provider choice and retains both Google and Microsoft relationships. Material variation lies in strategic emphasis. The Linklaters comparison treats concentrated partnerships such as A&O Shearman–Harvey and Clifford Chance–Microsoft as routes to deep integration or enterprise productivity that carry dependency or reduced-diversification risks. The Freshfields account instead presents integrated deployment within a deliberately diversified provider portfolio and adds client acceptance as a separate constraint on adoption, even where internal deployment is extensive. These curated sources therefore illuminate contrasting strategies rather than establishing how prevalent either approach was in 2025.

qs.q: He added:  > Obviously AI is built on cloud, but you can definitely have a cloud provider, or multiple cloud providers, and even multiple AI providers.
qs.a: How Freshfields is Building a Multi-Agent AI Strategy for Legal Workflows with Google Cloud · Market & press · 2025

elens.an: The curated 2026 sources support the proposition primarily by treating legal AI as governed enterprise infrastructure rather than a standalone model. Across the period, they emphasise connections to existing legal systems, inherited permissions, central governance, firm-specific knowledge, agentic execution and defined practitioner-review points. Freshfields adds reported evidence that this infrastructure model had moved into daily use at substantial organizational scale, supported by bespoke applications, security controls and training. Material variation concerns evidence and strategic risk: Google Cloud makes broad product and cost-capacity claims for a preview offering; Artificial Lawyer stresses intensified competition and specialist-provider partnerships; Freshfields documents uptake but not quantified gains in accuracy, cost or client outcomes. The sources therefore support the integration-benefit side much more directly than the proposition’s dependence side. Google asserts that its ecosystem avoids vendor lock-in, while these particular 2026 records do not independently test that assertion or substantiate governance fragility across connected systems.
